comment: Hand-cue systems the app can show alongside a sound. The app ships with NO cue content: each system here is a slot, and the videos that fill it live under cues/<system>/<accent>/ on the machine of whoever recorded them. 'publish' decides whether that content may enter a public repo — see scripts/check_cues.py, which fails a commit that would leak a restricted system.

systems.name: No hand cues
systems.note: The default. The app's own mouth diagrams and close-ups carry the articulation on their own.

systems.name: Cued Articulation (Jane Passy)

rights.holder: Jane Passy, John Botham and Helen Botham
rights.status: third-party — permission required before anything is published
rights.why: ACER Press publishes the books, posters, cards and its own Cued Articulation app. A free public copy of the full cue set substitutes for products they sell, which is the case most likely to draw a takedown. Using the cues in your own classroom is what the training is for; publishing a complete reference of them is a different act.
rights.ifGranted: Record the grant in this block (date, who, what it covers) and only then flip publish to true.

systems.note: AU and UK share the system; the vowel set differs because the cues map to phonemes and the two accents do not have the same ones.

systems.name: My own cues

rights.status: yours — publishable if you want them to be
rights.why: A cue set you devised yourself carries no one else's rights. This is the slot that can ship with the app.

systems.note: Same slot mechanics as any other system: drop videos in cues/own/<accent>/<phoneme id>.mp4 and they appear.
